newsitem.title: POLAND: ISUZU TO GET POLISH PLANT PERMIT IN APRIL.
newsitem.headline: ISUZU TO GET POLISH PLANT PERMIT IN APRIL.

text.p: Japan's Isuzu Motors Ltd, planning to build a 380 million mark diesel engine plant in a special economic zone in southern Poland, will get the necessary permit by the end of April, a zone official said.

Piotr Wojaczek, head of the management company running the zone, told Reuters the Japanese won a tender for a 34.5 hectare plot of land near the town of Tychy for the factory which would employ 400 workers and produce 300,000 engines annually.
Its annual sales are to be about one billion marks and the production would be exported to European Union countries.
"Within the next few days and by the end of the month at the latest Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek will issue a permit for the start of the Isuzu investment," Wojaczek said.
The engines will be designed for Opel passenger cars, made by General Motors' German subsidiary Adam Opel AG.
General Motors holds a 37.4-percent stake in Isuzu.
Setting up a business in the special economic zone exempts investors from Poland's 40 percent corporate income tax for 10 years and entitles to a 50 percent reduction of the tax in the next 10 years.
